title: Why Do Bulldozers Have a Claw on the Back?
description:
Look at the back of a big bulldozer and you will see something strange. A giant steel claw, hanging there like a scorpion's tail. Most people think the blade at the front is the whole machine. But on hard ground, the blade is useless without that claw. Today, eleven parts of a bulldozer, and why each one exists, starting with the claw.

Machine Reverse takes apart the machines you see every day and explains, part by part, why each one exists. This video covers 11 parts.

Chapters:
0:00 Intro
1:02 1. The claw on the back
2:11 2. The replaceable tooth
3:11 3. The raised sprocket
4:21 4. The curved blade
5:30 5. The steel tracks
6:35 6. The cage around the operator
7:42 7. The biggest bulldozer
8:50 8. The bulldozer pushing another machine
9:51 9. The armored bulldozer
10:48 10. The landfill tracks
11:50 11. The yellow paint
12:55 The verdict

Sources:
- Bulldozer parts (ripper, blades S/U/SU, tracks and grousers, undercarriage wear): Wikipedia, "Bulldozer" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bulldozer ; Caterpillar Performance Handbook
- Ripping vs blasting: Caterpillar, "Handbook of Ripping" https://www.cat.com/
- Elevated sprocket (introduced on the Cat D10, 1977): Wikipedia, "Caterpillar D10" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caterpillar_D10 ; Caterpillar history https://www.caterpillar.com/en/company/history.html
- ROPS / FOPS and seat belts: OSHA 29 CFR 1926.1001 ; NIOSH, "Preventing Injuries and Deaths from Rollovers"
- Komatsu D575A-3 Super Dozer (~152 t, 1,150 hp, ~69 m3 blade): Komatsu product data ; Wikipedia, "Komatsu D575A" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Komatsu_D575A
- Push-loading scrapers with dozers: Wikipedia, "Wheel tractor-scraper" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wheel_tractor-scraper
- Armored Caterpillar D9 (IDF): Wikipedia, "IDF Caterpillar D9" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IDF_Caterpillar_D9
- Landfill dozers and compaction: Caterpillar waste handling arrangements ; US EPA landfill guidance
- Caterpillar "Hi-Way Yellow" (December 1931): Caterpillar history https://www.caterpillar.com/en/company/history.html
